title: Distant M6.5+ earthquakes at 3 kPa or more raised rates for about 12 h in US geothermal areas, mainly The Geysers, Yellowstone and Long Valley, not in tectonic or injection areas (ComCat 1984-2026)
abstract: We tested remote dynamic triggering in 15 US regions with the public USGS ComCat catalogue for 1984-2026. The regions were in three groups that we set before the test: six geothermal and volcanic areas, five wastewater-injection areas and four tectonic controls. The triggers were 1,579 shallow M6.5+ earthquakes at 400 km or more. For each pair of a trigger and a region we estimated the peak dynamic stress with an Ms amplitude formula. We compared the event count after the surface-wave start with the rate in the 10 days before the origin. Placebo origins shifted by 5-120 days gave the null (1,000 for each pair). In the 3 h window, the geothermal group rate was 2.14 times the placebo median at 1 kPa or more (95% placebo range 0.77-1.58; p = 0.004; 523 pairs) and 4.11 times at 3 kPa or more (p = 0.006). The response grew with stress and was 6.95 times the background in the first hour, then decreased to the background by about 12 h. Tectonic controls did not respond (0.79 at 3 kPa or more; 95% upper limit 1.5). Injection areas gave no clear response (1.53, p = 0.052 at 1 kPa or more). The geothermal result stayed when we removed any one trigger or region, repeated with only 2005-2026 triggers (2.95, p = 0.018), and became stronger with magnitude cuts raised by 0.5. The Geysers, Yellowstone and Long Valley carried most of the response; Coso and the Salton Sea did not respond. In a post hoc split, triggers at 5,000 km or more (including Tohoku 2011 and Kamchatka 2025) did not raise rates at equal estimated stress. Limitations: the stress values are approximate, the catalogue misses many small triggered events, the injection test has low power at M1.5-2.0 cuts, and the distance result needs an independent test.
